菲利普·莫里斯一直严重依赖广告。1954年推出的万宝路牛仔——那个阳刚的牛仔吸烟者——立即获得成功（Barnet and Cavanagh 1994: 189–95）。1970年美国电视禁止香烟广告，这反而对万宝路牛仔有利，因为他在“大户外”中对自由的颂扬在广告牌上看起来格外好。公司高管坚信万宝路牛仔具有“全球”吸引力，同时也投入巨资进行市场研究，使万宝路形象更适合特定国家市场。例如在香港，这名牛仔在本地人看来像个地位卑微的劳工；菲利普·莫里斯撤掉了他，但保留了那匹马——对中国消费者而言，这是个有吸引力的形象。

In Indonesia, domestic cigarette producers were protected for many years by a national preference for clove cigarettes (i.e., tobacco cigarettes with cloves included as a flavoring). The challenge for foreign cigarette marketers was to create a new niche, with different tastes: The solution was an appeal to cosmopolitan youth, or at least their image, with its connotations of mobility, status, and urban distinction. In the United States, the public frowns on cigarette advertising directed toward youth. Yet Philip Morris was free to target anyone in Indonesia. And their market researchers had the examples of Gudang Garam’s and Bentoel’s advertising from which to develop their own billboard designs.
在印尼，国内香烟生产商多年来受到国民对丁香烟（即加入丁香作调味的烟草卷烟）偏好的保护。对外国香烟营销者而言，挑战是创造一种口味不同的新利基：解决办法是诉诸世界主义青年，或至少是他们的形象，连带其流动、地位和城市区分的含义。在美国，公众不赞成针对青年的香烟广告。然而菲利普·莫里斯在印尼可以自由锁定任何人。他们的市场研究员还有古当加拉姆和本托埃尔的广告作为范例，用来发展自己的广告牌设计。

It is in this context that Philip Morris created the “Marlboro adventure team” in 1994. Yearly contests picked national winners, not only from Indonesia, but also from Hong Kong, the Philippines, and Malaysia. Winners received a week of adventure sports in the U.S. West. While there was no direct rule against winners being female, all advertising, as well as photographs of past winners, showed men. As with Marlboro advertising in the United States, the contest evoked masculinity as the necessary prerequisite for the Great Outdoors; women were expected to consume as admirers of virile men.
正是在这种背景下，菲利普·莫里斯于1994年创建“万宝路冒险队”。年度比赛选出全国获胜者，不仅来自印尼，也来自香港、菲律宾和马来西亚。获胜者在美国西部体验一周冒险运动。虽然没有直接规定禁止女性获胜，但所有广告以及往届获胜者的照片都展示男性。如同万宝路在美国的广告，比赛把男性气概唤起为进入“大户外”的必要前提；女性则被期待作为阳刚男性的仰慕者来消费。

In 1997, Marlboro adventure team billboards were everywhere. Each showed a dramatic photograph of an adventure sport and offered the challenge: “Prove you have the daring!” Filmic versions were screened before every movie showing. Advertising brochures collected the photographs and sayings, as follows (all in Indonesian):
1997年，万宝路冒险队的广告牌随处可见。每一块都展示一项冒险运动的戏剧性照片，并提出挑战：“证明你有胆量！”电影版在每场电影放映前播放。广告宣传册汇集了这些照片和标语，如下（均为印尼语）：
Face the obstacles of savage nature. [A photograph shows dramatic lightning striking the U.S. southwest desert.] Are you brave enough to take control?
面对野蛮自然的障碍。[照片显示戏剧性的闪电劈向美国西南部沙漠。] 你有足够的勇气去掌控吗？[吉普车驶过沙漠。]
Tossed against terrifying rapids! [A wild river.] Are you brave enough with just a paddle? [A paddler steers in the spray.]
被抛入可怕的激流！[一条狂野的河流。] 只凭一支桨，你有足够的勇气吗？[一名桨手在浪花中掌舵。]
Your arena is risk. [Steep canyons.] Are you brave enough to subjugate it?
你的竞技场是风险。[陡峭的峡谷。] 你有足够的勇气征服它吗？[摩托车手腾空。]
Hundreds of meters high, hanging from a cliff! [A towering rock.] Are you brave enough with a single rope? [A climber hangs.]
数百米高，悬挂在崖壁上！[高耸的岩石。] 只凭一根绳子，你有足够的勇气吗？[一名攀岩者悬在空中。]
Reach for a field without a master. [Desert.] Are you brave enough to break through? [Mountain bikers. ]
奔向一片无主的旷野。[沙漠。] 你有足够的勇气突破吗？[山地自行车手。]
Sprint swiftly between steep hills. [Horses in the desert.] Are you brave enough to race? [Racing horsemen. ]
在陡峭山丘之间飞速冲刺。[沙漠中的马群。] 你有足够的勇气比赛吗？[赛马骑手。]

The spirit of these advertisements does not quite fit the nature lovers I knew: The advertisements focus on virility and risk, rather than the contemplative freedom of nature more important to nature lovers. Some of the fantasies the ad campaign invokes may have set out to appeal to other Asian audiences, as well as the advertisers’ own images of the outdoors. Yet it is hard to escape the connection between this campaign and the groundwork laid by Gudang Garam and Bentoel. Nature lovers were quick to tell me about these connections, as they formed a commercial lineage of selling nature lover identities.
这些广告的精神并不完全契合我认识的自然爱好者：广告着重阳刚之气和风险，而不是对自然爱好者更重要的自然沉思式自由。这场广告运动所唤起的一些幻想，也许意在吸引其他亚洲受众，以及广告商自己对户外的想象。然而，很难避开这场运动与古当加拉姆和本托埃尔打下的基础之间的联系。自然爱好者很快把这些联系告诉我，因为它们构成了一条贩卖自然爱好者身份的商业谱系。

Furthermore, nature lovers were excited by the popularization of their images in Marlboro advertising. Throughout the summer of 1997, Marlboro sponsored exhibitions in shopping malls advertising the adventure team campaign. The exhibitions were planned for twenty-six cities—with more than one in major cities—providing a reasonably precise map of Indonesia’s cosmopolitan centers. The exhibitions sold Marlboro products and advertised the contest. They displayed the wonders of adventure sports, complete, in some cases, with a climbing wall and demonstration dirt bikes. In some cities, they also provided a forum for nature lovers to get together to advertise themselves. Around the central Marlboro station in the Jakarta exhibition I visited, nature lovers set up tables presenting their offerings. Private clubs advertised their outdoor trips and training. Distributors advertised nature lover paraphernalia. Student nature clubs, too, set up tables to attract new members and tell others about their activities. The Marlboro campaign had organized a new confluence of nature loving concerns, presenting nature lovers with the opportunity to be entrepreneurs. Surprisingly, even the Indonesian Environmental Forum (WALHI) joined the Marlboro exhibition. The WALHI representative was not there to talk about the environmental problems of tobacco growing or smoking. As a panel participant, he introduced environmental advocacy; he was hoping, he said privately, to politicize nature lovers. Within the range of interests the exhibition promoted, advocacy was possible, too. If wild nature was a site of fashionable consumer identity, perhaps new activists could be recruited, along with athletes, romantics, and smokers.

此外，自然爱好者对自己形象在万宝路广告中的普及感到兴奋。1997年整个夏天，万宝路在购物中心赞助宣传冒险队活动的展览。展览计划在26个城市举办——主要城市不止一处——相当精确地描绘出印尼世界主义中心的分布图。展览销售万宝路产品并宣传比赛。它们展示冒险运动的奇观，有时还配有攀岩墙和示范越野摩托车。在一些城市，它们也为自然爱好者提供一个聚在一起宣传自己的论坛。在我参观的雅加达展览中，万宝路中心展台周围，自然爱好者摆起桌子展示他们的项目。私人俱乐部宣传其户外旅行和训练。经销商宣传自然爱好者用具。学生自然俱乐部也摆起桌子，吸引新成员并告诉别人他们的活动。万宝路活动组织了一个新的自然之爱关注汇流，为自然爱好者提供了成为企业家的机会。令人惊讶的是，连印尼环境论坛（WALHI）也加入了万宝路展览。那位 WALHI 代表来此并不是为了谈论烟草种植或吸烟的环境问题。作为小组成员，他介绍环境倡导；他私下说，他希望使自然爱好者政治化。在展览所推广的兴趣范围内，倡导也是可能的。如果野生自然是一个时尚消费身份的场所，那么也许除了运动员、浪漫主义者和吸烟者之外，还能招募到新的活动家。

The commercialization of nature lover imagery forms a clear example of what I am calling a contingent lineage of cosmopolitan specificity. The cigarette advertising campaigns that invoked nature loving built upon each other, drawing nature lovers into their plans. Gudang Garam’s initial success grew in large part from the chance event that Norman Edwin, as a widely read journalist and an admired mountain climber, was available to bring his personal charisma to the cigarette business. His accidental death increased his charisma, and gave a push to the second rock climbing ad campaign, as well as to Bentoel’s river-oriented take-off. Philip Morris was able to draw from the success of each of these Indonesian campaigns in presenting their cigarette as an element of outdoor adventures. Meanwhile, each of these campaigns popularized Indonesian nature loving, and they created new opportunities for consumer-oriented identity formation for would-be cosmopolitan youth. The consumerist lineage of nature loving grew from one unpredictable, contingent development to another. It converged, too, with other contingent lineages of nature loving, including those I have identified as anti-politics nationalism, urban distinctions, and adventure geographies. Together, they mapped the ground on which nature loving seemed exciting, popular, and able to address cosmopolitan yearnings. Various images of the challenge of nature were confused and blended, ranging from masculine self-assertion to rural nostalgia, and from individual freedom to environmental advocacy. I have suggested the limitations of this ground—as well as its openings and possibilities—in describing the Jakarta Marlboro exhibition, with its fashionable products, its eager student club recruiters, and its hopeful activists, as well as its transnational cigarette hustlers.

自然爱好者形象的商业化，为所谓世界主义特殊性的偶然谱系提供了一个清晰例子。唤起自然之爱的香烟广告运动彼此叠加，把自然爱好者卷入它们的计划。古当加拉姆最初的成功在很大程度上来自一个偶然事件：诺曼·埃德温作为广受阅读的记者和受人敬仰的登山者，恰好可以把他个人的魅力带入香烟生意。他的意外死亡增加了他的魅力，也推动了第二次攀岩广告运动，以及本托埃尔以河流为主题的仿效广告。菲利普·莫里斯能够借鉴这些印尼广告运动各自的成功，把其香烟呈现为户外冒险的元素。与此同时，这些运动普及了印尼的自然之爱，也为想要成为世界主义者的青年创造了以消费为导向的身份形成新机会。自然之爱的消费主义谱系从一次不可预测的偶然发展走向另一次。它也与其他偶然谱系汇合，包括我所说的反政治民族主义、城市区分和冒险地理。它们共同绘制出自然之爱显得激动人心、受欢迎并能回应世界主义渴望的基础。关于自然挑战的各种形象混杂交融，从男性自我主张到乡村怀旧，从个人自由到环境倡导。我在描述雅加达万宝路展览时——它有时尚产品、热切的学生俱乐部招募者、怀抱希望的活动家，以及跨国香烟贩子——已指出这一基础的局限，以及它的开口与可能。

Another of the Marlboro exhibitions of the summer of 1997 was planned for the city of Banjarmasin. It was never held; pre-election riots that spring burned down the main shopping mall and everything around it. At least one hundred and twenty-five people died in the burning shopping center, mysteriously piled into a heap; the government claimed they were looters. The commercial downtown was reduced to smoldering husks. It turned out that this event was a pre-figuration of things to come in Indonesia, as ethnic and political violence, often sparked by secret army provocations, spread. Neither commercial campaigns (like those of cigarette companies) nor individual voyages of self-discovery (like those of nature lovers) turned out to be as autonomous of state, regional, and ethnic politics as they imagined themselves under the protection of the New Order regime and its economic miracle. The convergence of contingent lineages that produced the nature loving I knew in the 1990s turned out to be tentative and unstable. Viewed through the hole in the Marlboro exhibition schedule left by the fires in Banjarmasin, one might see that its future was already unclear.

1997年夏天另一场万宝路展览原计划在班贾尔马辛举行。它从未举办；那年春天选举前的骚乱烧毁了主要购物中心及其周围一切。至少125人死在燃烧的购物中心里，尸体神秘地堆成一堆；政府声称他们是抢劫者。商业市中心被烧成冒烟的残骸。这场事件后来成为印尼未来的预示，族群与政治暴力——常常由军队的秘密挑衅引发——蔓延开来。无论是商业运动（如香烟公司的运动），还是个人自我发现之旅（如自然爱好者的旅行），都不像它们在新秩序政权及其经济奇迹保护下所想象的那样，独立于国家、区域和族群政治。产生我所熟悉的20世纪90年代自然之爱的那些偶然谱系汇流，结果是暂定的、不稳定的。透过班贾尔马辛大火在万宝路展览日程中留下的空洞来看，人们也许会发现，它的未来早已不确定。
without a sense of restlessness, dejection, or anxiety,
I am happy, relieved, and free,
—from a nature lovers’ club log book, 1993

With this much context established, I can return to my initial questions about the shape and feeling of “nature” among Indonesian nature lovers. Rather than continue to map trends and decode representations, I turn to things I learned directly from particular nature lovers. The contingent lineages I have described lay the social framework for nature loving, but they do not express the force of the sentiment of loving nature. They do not tell us how and why particular people are moved by the romance of nature. This requires asking individuals, whose personal trajectories work within the confluence of cultural lineages but make something personally meaningful of them.
——摘自自然爱好者俱乐部日志，1993
有了这么多背景，我可以回到最初关于印尼自然爱好者中“自然”的形态与感受的问题。我不再继续绘制趋势和解码表征，而是转向我从具体自然爱好者那里直接学到的东西。我描述的偶然谱系为自然之爱奠定了社会框架，却没有表达热爱自然这种情感的力量。它们没有告诉我们，特定的人如何以及为何被自然的浪漫打动。这需要询问个人，他们的个人轨迹在文化谱系的汇流中运作，却从中创造出对自己有意义的东西。

Let me introduce four nature lovers I had the chance to get to know in Yogya in 1997. Sri is a creative and energetic young woman, determined to find her personal path. Nature loving has opened her eyes to the wonder and majesty of the world. Budi is a mischievous young man, properly proud of his charm, his intellect, his openness to unconventional ideas, and his only-sometimes successful ability to get out of sticky situations. He offers his cheeky enthusiasm to nature lovers, inspiring the younger kids and keeping up the spirits of the old-timers. Dwi is serious, thoughtful, and religiously pious; he would like to see the nature lovers’ club become well-organized, well-documented, and successful. Hamam is on a larger personal and social mission: How can we improve both ourselves and the world? Through nature loving he has found a taste for the responsibilities and challenges of NGO work, as well as those of a disciplined personal spirituality.

让我介绍我1997年在日惹有机会认识的四个自然爱好者。斯里是一位有创造力、精力充沛的年轻女子，决心找到自己的个人道路。自然之爱让她睁开眼睛，看到世界的奇妙与壮丽。布迪是个调皮的年轻人，恰当地为自己的魅力、才智、对非正统观念的开放，以及只有时才奏效的脱困本领感到自豪。他把俏皮的激情献给自然爱好者，激励年轻孩子，也维持老成员的士气。德维严肃、深思、虔诚；他希望自然爱好者俱乐部组织良好、记录完整、取得成功。哈曼肩负着更大的个人与社会使命：我们如何改善自己和世界？通过自然之爱，他尝到了非政府组织工作的责任与挑战，也尝到了有纪律的个人灵性生活的滋味。

In many ways, these four young people, when I knew them, were no different than other students in Yogyakarta. They blended in easily: They were friendly, informal, good-looking, always ready to hang out and talk, and full of ideas and dreams. Like their outdoorsy counterparts in the United States and elsewhere, they were in excellent physical condition; they were articulate and upwardly mobile, at least in their imagination; if they had any potentially damaging eccentricities, they were still hidden behind the promise of youth. Like most nature lovers around the world, they are interesting not so much as personalities but as thinkers, organizers, leaders, or poets, able to articulate imagery or inspire activities that move others to appreciate the world around them. To meet them is to follow them into their ideas and projects. And so, I present them in the ethnographic present, and without much personal contextualization.

在许多方面，我认识这四个年轻人时，他们与日惹的其他学生并无不同。他们很容易融入：友善、随意、好看、随时愿意一起闲逛聊天，充满想法和梦想。像美国和其他地方热爱户外的同龄人一样，他们身体状况极佳；他们表达清晰、有向上流动的野心，至少在想象中如此；即使他们有任何可能造成损害的怪癖，也仍隐藏在青春的承诺背后。像世界各地大多数自然爱好者一样，他们之所以有趣，与其说在于个性，不如说在于他们是思考者、组织者、领导者或诗人，能够表达意象，或激励他人欣赏周围世界的活动。遇见他们，就是跟随他们进入他们的想法和计划。因此，我以民族志的现在时呈现他们，而且没有作太多个人背景交代。

It is Sri who speaks most forcefully about awe and the magic of nature. She wrote for me about mountains: “For me, the word mountain makes me mesmerized; I have the image of beauty, vastness, power, intimacy, companionship, and the mystery in it. Why? In my thinking, a mountain is a miracle of nature that cannot be defeated. It can erupt; it can shake the earth in a quake; it can lose a person who takes lightly the procedures for working together on the mountain; at the same time, it also hides so many secrets that humans can never uncover. The height of a mountain, the density of its forests, the cold of a mountain, the high peak: these are things that astonish me.”

I had asked Sri about the custom of climbing mountains at night to arrive at the peak at sunrise. She explained the stunning effect of the sunrise breaking over a vast panorama extended in time as well as space. “The moment I see the sunrise, the feeling in my heart is like being born again—and of meaning nothing as long as the world has existed. For the nature that exists at that instant was already there before I was born, and it will be there too after I die. Who knows from when and until when the sun has risen like that?”
最有力地谈论敬畏与自然魔力的人是斯里。她为我写下山：“对我而言，‘山’这个词令我着迷；我心中浮现出美、辽阔、力量、亲密、陪伴，以及其中的神秘。为什么？在我的想法里，山是自然不可战胜的奇迹。它会喷发；它会震动大地；它会让轻视山中协作规程的人迷失；与此同时，它还隐藏着如此多人类永远无法揭开的秘密。山的高度、森林的茂密、山中的寒冷、高耸的峰顶：这些都令我惊叹。”
我曾问斯里夜间登山、以便日出时抵达峰顶的习俗。她解释说，日出在广阔全景上破晓，其效果在时间和空间上都延伸开来，十分震撼。“看到日出的那一刻，我心中的感觉就像获得了重生——又像在世界存在的全部时间里，自己无足轻重。因为那一刻存在的自然，在我出生之前就已经在那里，在我死后也仍会在那里。谁知道太阳这样升起，是从何时开始，到何时结束？”

Sri writes poetry inspired by her experiences in nature. She depends on nature to help her work through life’s traumas and challenges. On the mountain, she explains, “I am like a student listening to my teacher who is telling me about how to live, a teacher who is instructing me but also a teacher who invites discussion, and I am given problems to finish myself, as well as perils.” She learns about nature’s needs as well as her own. “From the mountain I learn that it isn’t necessary to try to subjugate or exploit nature, whatever one’s purpose.” The mountain puts our petty goals and troubles in nature’s grand perspective. Nature is a site of wisdom and a source of healing. “From ‘studying about nature’ we should also ‘study in nature’ at the same time as ‘studying from nature.”

斯里受自然中的经历启发写诗。她依靠自然帮助自己度过人生的创伤与挑战。她解释说，在山上，“我像一个学生，听老师讲如何生活；这位老师既指导我，也邀我讨论，还给我需要自己解决的问题，也让我面对危险。”她了解自然的需要，也了解自己的需要。“从山那里我学到，无论目的是什么，都不必试图征服或开发自然。”山以自然的宏大视角，让我们琐碎的目标和烦恼显出本来面目。自然是智慧的场所，也是疗愈的源泉。“从‘研究自然’中，我们也应当同时‘在自然中学习’和‘向自然学习’。”

Studying from nature can also mean studying from the “local people,” those closer to the natural world and its archaic, mysterious wisdom. I found Sri’s story of her 1991 ascent of Mount Lawu in central Java particularly moving as it told of her awkward but intense engagement with a Javanese villager she met at the summit. Sri was able to engage this villager because of her romance with nature. Even as she processed the encounter through this romance, nature loving also became a way to reach out and to evaluate her cosmopolitan difference.
向自然学习，也可以意味着向“当地人”学习——那些更接近自然世界及其古老、神秘智慧的人。我觉得斯里关于1991年攀登中爪哇拉武山的故事尤其动人，因为它讲述了她与一位在山顶遇到的爪哇村民笨拙却强烈的接触。斯里能够与这位村民交流，是因为她对自然的浪漫。即使她通过这种浪漫来消化这次相遇，自然之爱也成为她向外伸手并评估自己世界主义差异的方式。

It all began, she explained, when she and a group of nature lovers climbed Mount Lawu on the first day of the Javanese month of Suro, the date of an important traditional festival for which many people gather on the mountain. “So many people were climbing Mount Lawu! At the summit of the mountain, there were people selling meatball soup and hot tea and coffee. They had stoves there and had been living there for a week!

“I became fascinated by the people who had climbed the mountain. They had come wearing regular jackets and caps. They sat there quietly, in reflection within themselves. And they were only wearing [thin cloth] sarongs! While we mountain climbers had come with large backpacks, with secure hiking boots, with camping stoves, with sleeping bags, with tents. And even then we moaned, ‘Oh, this’ and ‘Oh, that’ and every kind of ‘Oh my.’
“But they had come only with their own bodies and maybe a bottle of water. So I ventured to ask—not really an interview, but I wanted to ask—one of the men, using Javanese:
‘Why, sir, have you come here? Isn’t it cold?’
她解释说，这一切始于她和一群自然爱好者在爪哇历苏罗月第一天攀登拉武山；那天有一个重要的传统节日，许多人会聚集在山上。“那么多人攀登拉武山！在山顶，有人卖肉丸汤、热茶和咖啡。他们带着炉子，已经在那里住了一个星期！
“我迷上了那些登山的人。他们穿着普通夹克，戴着帽子。他们安静地坐着，沉浸于内心默想。而他们只穿着（薄布）纱笼！我们这些登山者却带着大背包、结实登山靴、露营炉、睡袋和帐篷。即便如此，我们还抱怨‘哎呀这个’‘哎呀那个’，各种‘我的天’。
“但他们只带着自己的身体，也许还有一瓶水。于是我壮着胆子——不算真正采访，但我想问——用爪哇语问其中一位：
‘先生，您为什么来这里？不冷吗？’

‘My dear, this is the way I can offer prayers for my children. So that my children can become someone. So that they can work well. So that they won’t encounter difficulties. So that they will be able to get money for their work.

Yes, it’s only this that I can do for my children. So that nothing terrible will happen. I’m not a rich man. I can only make a plea for a blessing. I pray for all my family, my children, and myself for the gift of happiness.’
‘亲爱的，这是我能为孩子们祈祷的方式。好让我的孩子们能成为人物。好让他们工作顺利。好让他们不遇困难。好让他们能靠工作挣到钱。
是的，我只能为孩子们做这些。好让什么可怕的事都不发生。我不是有钱人。我只能祈求赐福。我为全家人、孩子们和自己祈求幸福的恩赐。’
‘But, sir, why are you only wearing a sarong?’
‘可是，先生，您为什么只穿一条纱笼？’

‘My dear, if things are already as they are, what is one’s body? Cold is also given by the Almighty. If we are warm, that is also given by the Almighty. This is what I have to enjoy. I have this sarong, and what else is needed?’

“All that I could think was, well, yes, I’m not embarrassed, it’s true I have a full load of equipment, and it gives me security. But like that—simple—I could carry just a little money—every day one only needs to eat maybe two times and drink tea or coffee one or two times—I would need perhaps only Rp. 1,000 to eat because they are selling food here. And, with just that, it would be enough for me.

“My heart’s approach—I can’t translate it into words. Well, I thought, this is a different approach to life. And I kept thinking: Next year, if I can, I want to join a ritual occasion like this. I want to have little, as they do. I won’t be trifling. I won’t climb the mountain for show, with a backpack and a full set of equipment.”
‘亲爱的，事情既然已经这样，身体算什么呢？寒冷也是全能者赐予的。如果我们暖和，那也是全能者赐予的。这是我必须享受的。我有这条纱笼，还需要什么呢？’
“我能想到的只有：嗯，是的，我并不感到难为情，我确实带着满满一包装备，它给我安全感。但像那样——简简单单——我可以只带一点钱——每天只需吃两顿，喝一两次茶或咖啡——我在这里买吃的，也许只需要1000印尼盾。那样对我就够了。
“我内心的这种接近方式——我无法用语言翻译出来。嗯，我想，这是另一种对待生活的方式。我一直在想：明年，如果可能，我想参加一次这样的仪式活动。我想像他们那样，拥有得很少。我不会敷衍了事。我不会为了炫耀，背着背包和全套装备去登山。”

The encounter continued to teach Sri about life. The next year she did reclimb Mount Lawu by herself, seeking a time of introspection and reflection. It was a spiritual journey in which she went to “receive the power of nature.” And, even in growing beyond the ardors of active nature loving, she has continued to learn from nature.
这次相遇继续教给斯里关于生活的事。第二年，她独自重登拉武山，寻求一段内省与反思的时光。这是一次灵性之旅，她去“接受自然的力量”。即使在超越活跃的自然之爱所带来的热情之后，她仍继续向自然学习。

Although nature is also a place of personal growth for Budi, he finds it not so much a sacred site as a site for exploring personal freedom. He started nature loving as a rebellious high school student. “The first time I climbed Mount Merapi,” he explained, “I hardly remember it, I was drunk, I was with other high school students trying to reach Mount Vodka.” He wanted to be an “outlaw,” and he found free-spirited—and often drunk—community with nature lovers. Even in college, he turned to nature loving to find a good time outside the boundary of dull respectability. He jokes about it with a sense of self-mocking irony: “In my college, my friends did nothing but study. Oh shit, no fun [This in English]. So I made a connection with the upperclassmen who already were the informal power in the college. We had beautiful moments. While they were studying, I was laughing and making jokes. And I still got good grades.”

尽管自然对布迪来说也是个人成长之地，但他觉得它与其说是圣地，不如说是探索个人自由的场所。他作为反叛的高中生开始自然之爱。“第一次攀登默拉皮山，”他解释说，“我几乎不记得了，我喝醉了，和其他高中生一起，想登上伏特加山。”他想成为“法外之徒”，并在自然爱好者中找到了自由奔放——而且常常醉酒——的社群。即使在大学里，他也转向自然之爱，在沉闷体面生活的边界之外寻找快乐。他带着自嘲式的反讽开玩笑说：“在大学里，我的朋友们除了学习什么也不做。哦，妈的，没劲［原文为英语］。所以我与高年级同学建立了联系，他们已经是学院里的非正式权力。我们有过美好的时光。他们在学习时，我在大笑、讲笑话。而我的成绩仍然很好。”

I found Budi’s ability to laugh at his own weaknesses—and those of his mates—to be one of his most attractive qualities. In telling his personal history with nature loving, he stressed the transgressive quality of the groups he joined, as well as the superficiality of their obsessions with oppositional style. He tells of a mountain climbing club he joined: “We were the hoodlums of the campus. We took on a tough appearance. We acted hard and stubborn. But in practice, we were lazy.” When they hiked, they rarely got above the settlements of local residents. “It was just a tourist trip.” But they thought of themselves as brave adventurers: “We had to go to places that were exotic and romantic.” Meanwhile, the club’s membership and its standing in the school grew. “We had a kind of power—social status and reasonably nice bodies.” They bullied the college to give them funds for their trips: “If nothing was forthcoming, we would say, ‘Take our request to the Assistant Deacon, or we will badmouth you.’” They got all kinds of funds and support, and used them to play. “At that time, we were hedonists, and we loved to have a good time.”

我发现布迪嘲笑自己弱点——以及同伴弱点——的能力，是他最有魅力的品质之一。在讲述自己与自然之爱的个人历史时，他强调自己所加入群体的越轨性质，以及他们对对抗性风格的痴迷之肤浅。他谈到自己加入的一个登山俱乐部：“我们是校园里的流氓。我们摆出强硬的样子。我们装作强悍固执。但实际上，我们很懒。”徒步时，他们很少走到当地居民聚落之上。“那只是一次游客旅行。”但他们把自己想象成勇敢的冒险者：“我们必须去异域而浪漫的地方。”与此同时，俱乐部成员增加，在学校的地位也提高。“我们有一种权力——社会地位和还算不错的身材。”他们胁迫学院给他们旅行经费：“如果迟迟没有消息，我们就会说：‘去跟院长助理说我们的请求，否则我们就说你坏话。’”他们得到各种经费和支持，并用来玩乐。“那时我们是享乐主义者，我们喜欢玩得开心。”

Budi looks back on these early days and laughs at himself. He is a great commentator who has a way with words; he has something to say about every outing. In an interview about a nature lovers’ expedition to Lore Lindu, in the interior of Sulawesi, he was candid about the horrors of the trip, and particularly those involving the problems of social interaction on the team. In his self-conscious style, he was willing to blame himself as much as others for the tensions and to see the working out of these kinds of problems as part of the “experience” (pengalaman). He began his description with an awkward admission: “I didn’t want to go because the leader was Chinese. In those days I was racist against Chinese. I didn’t like them. A month before the departure, they still didn’t have a photographer.... So I went along.” Rather than a long-awaited romantic quest, the trip was an almost casual last-minute concession.

布迪回望这些早期日子，嘲笑自己。他是个很会说话的评论者；每次出游他都有话可说。在一次关于前往苏拉威西内陆洛雷林杜的自然爱好者探险的采访中，他坦率谈到旅途的恐怖，尤其是涉及团队社交互动问题的那部分。以他自觉的风格，他愿意为紧张关系既责怪别人也责怪自己，并把这些问题的解决视为“经验”（pengalaman）的一部分。他以一个尴尬的坦白开始描述：“我不想去，因为领队是华人。那时我歧视华人。我不喜欢他们。出发前一个月，他们还没有摄影师……所以我就去了。”这次旅行并非期待已久的浪漫追寻，而几乎是最后一刻随随便便的让步。

The social difficulties did not end with the constitution of the team. “There was lots of personal friction that emerged. I slept outside.... I slept in a hammock. I wanted to listen to the radio, and the radio was inside [the tent], but I wasn’t allowed inside. Saiful, a Palembang guy, didn’t want to come out; he wasn’t brave enough. ‘If you come out, I will really slash you with a machete.’ I was already annoyed but not yet insane. I smoked; I played gableg dominos constantly. We were almost a month in the forest. We really had to work in the forest.”

“It was alright. I had never been in the forest for so long. I had often been out for two, three, maybe four days. With the same people, looking for a new experience. Here the team interaction was different; my psychological condition was different.” He began to tell stories of the weird things they did. “We arrived at the peaks of that mountain range, and we stopped. We were to do research for two or three days. There we celebrated [a Muslim holiday] by butchering a chicken. We had a voodoo ritual...

We slaughtered it in a ceremony: ‘Wu wu wu, wu wu wu!’ [He danced around, mimicking old U.S. movie stereotypes of Native American ceremonies.] We circled around until that chicken must have been dizzy, in that party. Then we roasted it.”
社交困难并没有随着队伍组建而结束。“出现了很多个人摩擦。我睡在外面……我睡在吊床里。我想听收音机，收音机在［帐篷］里面，但我不被允许进去。萨伊富尔，一个巨港人，不愿出来；他不够胆量。‘你出来，我就真的用砍刀劈你。’我已经恼火，但还没发疯。我抽烟；我不断地玩 gableg 多米诺骨牌。我们在森林里待了将近一个月。我们真的得在森林里干活。”
“还行。我从未在森林里待这么久。我常常出去两天、三天，也许四天。和同样的人一起，寻找新体验。这里团队互动不同；我的心理状态也不同。”他开始讲述他们做的怪事。“我们到达那座山脉的峰顶，停了下来。我们要做两三天研究。我们在那里庆祝［一个穆斯林节日］，宰了一只鸡。我们举行了一场巫毒仪式……
我们在一个仪式中宰了它：‘呜 呜 呜，呜 呜 呜！’［他跳着舞，模仿美国老电影对美洲原住民仪式的刻板印象。］在那个聚会上，我们围着那只鸡转，想必把它转晕了。然后我们把它烤了。”

The bizarre, the crazy, the difficult, the intense: all were gathered in his experience. Interactions with the local villagers added to the mix. “Many times when we were hiking, we got lost. Once when we came into a village, we received a kind welcome.... When we arrived, we wanted to bathe. ‘There’s no bathroom, only in the river’ [the villagers said apologetically]. We went as a group down to the river to bathe, but the water was chocolate colored and nauseating. I figured they also bathed there [and bathed anyway]. When we finished bathing and went back to the village, they were laughing: ‘Ha, ha, taken in by a trick, taken in by a trick.’ That was crude.”
怪异、疯狂、艰难、强烈：全都汇入他的经验。与当地村民的互动又增添了混杂性。“徒步时我们常常迷路。有一次我们走进一个村庄，受到热情欢迎……到达时，我们想洗澡。‘没有浴室，只有河里能洗’［村民们抱歉地说］。我们一群人下河洗澡，但河水是巧克力色，令人恶心。我猜他们也在那里洗澡［还是洗了］。我们洗完澡回到村里时，他们哈哈大笑：‘哈，哈，上当了，上当了。’那很粗野。”

Sometimes, the nature lovers purposely took advantage of the villagers, too, as in this anecdote about a church auction, in which local people donated foodstuff to raise money for the church. “When we started to bid, no one was brave enough to bid higher than we did. So we could buy a chicken for Rp. 750 when they normally sold for two or three thousand rupiah. No one else would bid, so the chicken would go to us.”
有时自然爱好者也故意占村民便宜，比如下面这则关于教堂拍卖的轶事，当地人捐赠食物为教堂筹款。“我们开始出价时，没人敢出得比我们高。所以我们能用750印尼盾买下一只鸡，而它们通常卖两三千印尼盾。没有别人出价，所以鸡就归我们了。”

In the process of negotiation of their local status, Budi did learn some important things about social and environmental problems in the area. He went on to speak about the difficulties of organizing a national park into a protected core area and outlying buffer zones in which certain economic activities were permitted. A village had to be moved from the core and reestablished, with difficulty, on other land; the villagers were appropriately worried about schistosomiasis in their new location. His new knowledge and his endurance of the difficulties went hand in hand: As Budi explained, this was “experience.”
在协商其地方地位的过程中，布迪确实了解到该地区一些重要的社会与环境问题。他接着谈到把国家公园组织成受保护核心区与外围缓冲区的困难，后者允许某些经济活动。一个村庄不得不从核心区迁出，艰难地在另一块土地上重建；村民们理所当然地担心新地点的血吸虫病。他的新知识与他对困难的忍耐携手并进：正如布迪所解释，这就是“经验”。

Dwi was a member of this same expedition, and the trip also forms an important memory for him: a memory of a complex organizational undertaking. Dwi and Budi are close friends, but they have quite different styles. Dwi is serious, responsible, and meticulous, with none of Budi’s playful abandon. He showed me his diary from the Lore Lindu trip, which records every meal he ate, however humble, every social interaction that disturbed team dynamics, and every sleepless night spent swatting at mosquitoes. Even in his oral account, he narrated the trip as a series of technical failures and successes. He had some funny stories—a team member running from a snake; an unchewable piece of dried buffalo meat—and some moving stories, such as that of helping a “bewitched,” dehydrated villager through his knowledge of first aid. He attributes the problems they had, becoming lost in the forest, to an accumulation of technical mistakes, such as their casualness in taking compass readings, which could have prevented them from circling back on their tracks.

德维也是这次探险的成员，这次旅行对他同样构成一段重要记忆：一段关于复杂组织任务的记忆。德维和布迪是密友，但风格大不相同。德维严肃、负责、一丝不苟，没有布迪那种嬉闹的放纵。他给我看洛雷林杜之行的日记，其中记录他吃过的每一顿饭，无论多么简陋；每一次扰乱团队动态的社交互动；每一个拍打蚊子无法入睡的夜晚。即使口头叙述，他也把旅行讲成一连串技术失败与成功。他有些有趣的故事——一名队员躲蛇逃跑；一块嚼不烂的水牛肉干——也有些动人故事，比如他凭借急救知识帮助一位“中了邪”、脱水的村民。他把他们在森林中迷路的问题归因于一连串技术错误，例如，他们读取指南针时过于随意；认真读取本来可以防止他们兜圈子、又绕回走过的地方。

More recently, Dwi has become excited about the project of writing about nature lovers’ organizations. He has combed through available club records, compiling careful genealogies of club organization and activities. He also writes about nature lover objectives and training methods. So far, most of his writing has been circulated only internally among nature lovers; but he is thinking of other ways to use this material, not only to communicate about nature loving, but also to develop his skills as a communicator. Dwi is selfconscious about improving his writing, his management skills, and his technical knowledge through nature loving. For Dwi, nature is a site for building organizational leadership skills.
最近，德维对写作自然爱好者组织这件事感到兴奋。他仔细翻查可得的俱乐部记录，编纂俱乐部组织与活动的详细谱系。他也写自然爱好者的目标与训练方法。迄今为止，他的大部分写作只在自然爱好者内部流传；但他正在考虑用这些材料的其他方式，不仅为了沟通自然之爱，也为了发展自己作为沟通者的技能。德维自觉地通过自然之爱改进自己的写作、管理技能和技术知识。对德维来说，自然是建立组织领导能力的场所。

Hamam also feels a sense of social responsibility in nature. But for Hamam, the responsibility has nothing to do with the organizational features of nature lovers’ clubs. Hamam wants to improve himself and the world. Out in wild nature, Hamam says he feels his daily burdens lifted; and from this sense of relief, he feels he can come back to the city with a stronger sense of personal responsibility. After some time exploring nature loving, Hamam has also become interested in Javanese mysticism and started to work with a traditional mystic in training himself in that discipline. He has food taboos, such as not eating salt, which help him focus on personal growth. Nature loving also participates in his spiritual development. When he climbs a mountain by himself, he says he feels small. There are so many mysteries of nature that are unknown and difficult to understand with logical reason, even the idea that God or some Essence made the world. These kinds of thoughts do not make him want to remove himself from society; instead, they reaffirm his commitment to society—and to nature.

哈曼在自然之中也感到一种社会责任。但对哈曼来说，这种责任与自然爱好者俱乐部的组织特征无关。哈曼想改善自己和世界。哈曼说，置身野生自然，他感到日常负担被卸下；从这种解脱感中，他觉得自己可以带着更强的个人责任感回到城市。在探索自然之爱一段时间后，哈曼也对爪哇神秘主义产生兴趣，并开始跟随一位传统神秘主义者修习这门功夫。他有饮食禁忌，比如不吃盐，这帮助他专注于个人成长。自然之爱也参与他的灵性发展。他说，独自登山时，他感到自己渺小。自然有如此多未知的奥秘，难以用逻辑理性理解，甚至上帝或某种本质创造世界这一观念也是如此。这类想法并不使他想要脱离社会；相反，它们重申他对社会——以及对自然——的承诺。

Hamam feels that the term “nature loving” (kepencintaalaman) is a heavy burden that must be taken seriously. To love nature means to refuse to fight against nature. It means to guard nature and to unite oneself with nature. Most nature lovers, including himself, he says, are really just “enjoyers of nature” (penikmat alam). He, for example, still smokes; if he really would be a nature lover, he would have to give up smoking, he says. Loving nature is something to aspire to, not to claim easily.
哈曼觉得“自然之爱”（kepencintaalaman）一词是必须认真对待的沉重负担。爱自然意味着拒绝与自然抗争。它意味着守护自然，与自然合而为一。他说，大多数自然爱好者，包括他自己，其实只是“自然的享受者”（penikmat alam）。例如，他仍然吸烟；他说，如果他真要成为自然爱好者，就必须戒烟。爱自然是值得追求的事，而不是可以轻易自称的事。

Over the last few years, Hamam has become interested in environmental advocacy, either with established NGOs or with one he would organize himself. He has done some work with an NGO that advocates ecotourism as a socially responsible form of tourism. Mass tourism, Hamam says, drains the country’s natural resources. Tourism needs to be organized with conservation principles in mind. This could include educating tourists about the importance of natural ecosystems. He sees ecotourism, too, as a possible alternative to the natural and social destruction of most rural development projects. He told me of the horrors of the grand “One Million Hectares” development scheme that was a government showcase in 1996 in Central Kalimantan. He spent several months there, working as a community organizer advocating community-based ecotourism development. Government development plans made it difficult to get people to think in terms of small-scale alternatives. Planners had mapped out a huge tract of swampy country—one million hectares—to turn into wet-rice fields. The residents had had a profitable livelihood raising water buffaloes; the water buffaloes were all confiscated and taken away, leaving the people without resources. Meanwhile, the rice would not grow, he said. When the president came for a tour of the project, project managers took strips of sod with rice seedlings in it and laid them out, making it look as if this would be a fertile rice basket. As soon as the president left, the imported seedlings died, leaving the ground bare. Hamam sees this kind of large-scale irresponsibility as the major threat to the Indonesian environment.

过去几年，哈曼对环境倡导产生兴趣，无论是与现有非政府组织合作，还是自己组织一个。他曾与一个倡导生态旅游、视之为对社会负责的旅游形式的非政府组织合作。哈曼说，大众旅游榨干国家的自然资源。旅游组织必须考虑保护原则。这可能包括教育游客认识自然生态系统的重要性。他也把生态旅游视为替代大多数乡村发展项目所造成自然与社会破坏的可能方案。他向我讲述1996年中加里曼丹一个政府样板工程——宏伟的“百万公顷”开发计划——的恐怖。他在那里待了几个月，担任社区组织者，倡导以社区为基础的生态旅游发展。政府发展计划让人很难从替代性小规模方案的角度思考。规划者划出一大片沼泽地——100万公顷——要改成水稻田。居民原本靠养水牛获得颇丰收入；水牛全被没收带走，让人民失去资源。他说，与此同时，水稻长不起来。总统来项目视察时，项目经理把带着秧苗的草皮条铺开，弄得看起来这里将成为一个肥沃的稻米仓。总统一走，移来的秧苗就死了，留下光秃秃的土地。哈曼把这种大规模不负责任视为印尼环境的主要威胁。

Hamam’s interest in the NGO world brings me back to the relationship between nature loving and environmental advocacy. Nature, for Hamam, is a realm that calls up responsibility for better behavior. This is one way that nature loving can make environmental advocacy possible. But nature, for nature lovers, is a realm of many meanings and avenues for passion and growth. Sri’s wisdom and healing; Budi’s freedom and mobility; Dwi’s organizational aptitudes; and Hamam’s responsible guardianship: Each of these represents one of the ways nature comes to be a substantial thing in the nature loving community. There are diverse paths here. But each contributes to understandings of nature that might make one want to consider it an object of reflection, discussion, or advocacy.

哈曼对非政府组织世界的兴趣，把我带回到自然之爱与环保倡导的关系。对哈曼来说，自然是一个唤起更好行为责任的领域。这是自然之爱使环保倡导成为可能的一种方式。但对自然爱好者来说，自然是充满多种意义、激情与成长途径的领域。斯里的智慧与疗愈；布迪的自由与流动；德维的组织才能；哈曼负责任的守护：每一种都代表自然在自然爱好者社群中成为实质性事物的一种方式。这里有多种路径。但每一条都促成对自然的理解，使人可能想要把它视为反思、讨论或倡导的对象。

Nature loving is not the same as environmental activism. ‘The distinctiveness of student nature loving is, however, important to understanding environmentalism not only because many Indonesian environmental activists got their start in college nature loving, but also because they know how to recognize “the environment” in part because of nature loving. Further: Around the world, environmental activism depends on distinctive cultural ways of recognizing the environment. “Global environmentalism”—whether coercive or collaborative—can only exist in the dialogues and overlaps among these distinctive concerns about nature.
自然之爱并不等同于环保活动主义。然而，学生自然之爱的独特性对理解环保主义很重要，不仅因为许多印尼环保活动家从大学自然之爱起步，也因为他们部分依靠自然之爱才懂得如何识别“环境”。进一步说：在世界各地，环保活动主义依赖于识别环境的独特文化方式。“全球环保主义”——无论强制还是协作——只能存在于这些独特自然关切之间的对话与重叠中。

One important strain of nature appreciation in the United States naturalizes the love of nature to argue that it is a biological feature of human nature to feel refreshed in the wild (Kellert and Wilson 1993). This is the reason, many conservation biologists argue, that humans have a species responsibility to save nature. Indeed, it appears that the romance of nature is a widespread practice. Yet we need not naturalize it as a universal biology in order to appreciate its global spread. I have tried to show the formation of nature loving’s national particularities as a way of knowing its cosmopolitanism. The personal force of “nature,” and its appearance as an object of reflection, depends on both this localization and its cosmopolitan referents.

美国自然欣赏的一条重要脉络把对自然的热爱自然化，论证在野外感到精神焕发是人性的生物学特征（Kellert and Wilson 1993）。许多保护生物学家论证，这正是人类负有拯救自然之物种责任的原因。确实，自然的浪漫似乎是一种广泛传播的实践。然而，我们不必把它自然化为普遍生物学，才能欣赏其全球传播。我已试图书写自然之爱民族特殊性的形成，以此理解其世界主义。“自然”的个人力量，以及它作为反思对象的出现，既取决于这种地方化，也取决于它的世界主义指涉。
